match.reason: No single bank point compares plant and animal cells: the plant card covers only plant-specific parts, the animal card covers only animal parts, and neither mentions mitochondria, so the comparison needs a new point.

draft.title: Plant and animal cells compared
card: Both
Plant and animal cells each have a nucleus, a cell membrane, cytoplasm and mitochondria. These parts do the same jobs in both.
Cell wall
Plant cells have a stiff cell wall outside the cell membrane. It gives the cell support and shape. Animal cells have no cell wall.
Chloroplasts
Plant cells that carry out photosynthesis have chloroplasts, which capture light energy to make food. Animal cells have no chloroplasts.
Large vacuole
A mature plant cell has a large vacuole filled with fluid. It stores water and other substances. Animal cells lack a large vacuole like this.
draft.remember: Plant cells have all the animal cell parts plus a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

a.q: Which structure is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
opts: Chloroplasts
Mitochondria
Nucleus
Cytoplasm
a.why: Chloroplasts capture light energy for photosynthesis, and animal cells do not have them. Mitochondria are tempting, but both plant and animal cells have them.
a.clue: Which part is used for photosynthesis?

b.q: Under a microscope, Leila sees a cell with a nucleus, a cell membrane, cytoplasm and mitochondria, but no cell wall and no chloroplasts. What can she say about the cell?
opts: It could be an animal cell
It must be a plant cell
It cannot be a living cell
It is a plant cell without a nucleus
b.why: Animal cells have exactly these parts and lack a cell wall and chloroplasts, so it could be an animal cell. It cannot be said to be a plant cell, because plant cells have a cell wall.
b.clue: Check which parts are shared and which only plants have.

wants.brief: Two labelled cell diagrams side by side. Plant cell: cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts, large vacuole. Animal cell: cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria.
wants.why: Seeing both cells together shows which parts are shared and which only the plant cell has.

b.best: It could be an animal cell

problems.detail: The remember line says plant cells have chloroplasts and a large vacuole without qualification. The card says only plant cells that carry out photosynthesis have chloroplasts, and only mature plant cells have a large vacuole. Root cells, for example, have no chloroplasts, so the remember line overstates what the card teaches.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and their intended answers are correct. The remember line overgeneralises: it implies every plant cell has chloroplasts and a large vacuole, while the card limits these to photosynthesising and mature plant cells.
